h1: Dealing Ranges: Marking the Range That Matters
seoTitle: Dealing Ranges: Marking the Range That Matters | LearnSMC
metaDescription: Learn how to anchor an external dealing range between a sweep and a displacement leg, divide Premium vs. Discount at 50% EQ, and avoid stale ranges.
quickAnswer: A Dealing Range is the active price boundary anchored between a significant swing low and swing high—formed after a liquidity sweep and opposing displacement—divided at 50% Equilibrium into Discount (below) and Premium (above).
takeaways: Anchor a dealing range from the extreme of a liquidity sweep to the opposing extreme created by the displacement leg.
The 50% midpoint (Equilibrium) separates Discount (below 50%) from Premium (above 50%).
Internal ranges live inside external dealing ranges; always mark the higher-timeframe dealing range first.
When candle bodies close decisively beyond the anchored high or low, update your dealing range rather than clinging to stale anchors.

sections.title: 1. Why Every Setup Depends on the Right Dealing Range

blocks.text: Without an anchored Dealing Range, terms like Premium, Discount, and Optimal Trade Entry (OTE) have no fixed ruler. Drawing a Fibonacci grid from random highs and lows produces random percentages. A valid dealing range defines the exact battlefield between two confirmed structural extremes.

At its core, a Dealing Range answers one practical question before every study: am I looking at a cheap price (Discount, below 50% Equilibrium) or an expensive price (Premium, above 50% Equilibrium)? Measure the range wick-to-wick from the swing origin to the opposing displacement extreme; deeper Optimal Trade Entry (OTE) retracements (62%–79%) sit inside Deep Discount or Upper Premium.

sections.title: 6. External Dealing Range vs. Internal Sub-Range

blocks.text: A 15-minute dealing range often sits completely inside a 4-hour dealing range. Knowing whether price is in 4-hour Premium or Discount prevents taking a 15-minute Discount long directly into a 4-hour Premium resistance wall.

faqs.question: How do you anchor a Dealing Range properly?
faqs.answer: Anchor it from the extreme of a completed liquidity sweep (or swing origin) to the opposing confirmed swing extreme formed by the subsequent displacement leg.

faqs.question: What does 50% Equilibrium mean in a Dealing Range?
faqs.answer: Equilibrium is the exact 50% midpoint between Range Low and Range High, dividing Discount (below 50%) from Premium (above 50%).

faqs.question: When do you update a Dealing Range?
faqs.answer: Update the dealing range once candle bodies close decisively beyond the anchored high or low, forming a new displacement leg and opposing swing extreme.
